query: Earlier refractory high-entropy alloys illustrate persistent trade-offs: MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW retained good yield strength from 600 to 1600 °C, with MoNbTaVW reaching 842 MPa at 1000 °C, but both had poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density; HfNbTaTiZr showed room-temperature ductility above 50% and a yield strength of 929 MPa but only 295 MPa at 1000 °C; and as-cast HfMoTaTiZr achieved about 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at elevated temperature but retained a density of 10.21 g cm−3. Given the constraint that density must be reduced without sacrificing the strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, what single intervention should be tested? Provide a mechanistic hypothesis, predicted outcomes relative to the as-cast baseline, explicit temperature and loading boundary conditions, supporting evidence from the preceding RHEA results, and a controlled experiment with quantitative rejection criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of heavy Hf with a proportion of lighter Al in the as‐cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy will reduce the overall density without sacrificing the strong room‐ and high‐temperature mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast refractory high-entropy alloy HfMoTaTiZr (density ~10.21 g/cm3, RT yield strength ~1600 MPa, elevated yield strength ~855 MPa)
generation.intervention: Replace a controlled fraction of Hf by Al to form a modified composition (e.g. Hf1-xAlxMoTaTiZr with x around 0.1–0.3)
generation.conditions: Mechanical testing under room temperature and at elevated temperature (~1000 °C) loading conditions similar to those tested for the baseline alloy
generation.structural_mediator: The retention of the primary disordered BCC (or B2) solid solution matrix with similar lattice distortion and dislocation slip behavior, despite compositional change
generation.mechanism: Al has a lower atomic weight than Hf, so its partial substitution will lower the alloy density. Concurrently, if the solid solution and dislocation-mediated strengthening mechanisms are preserved, the alloy’s high yield strengths at room and elevated temperatures should be maintained.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy is expected to show an approximately 15% decrease in density while maintaining yield strengths within about 10% of the original values (i.e. near 1600 MPa at RT and 855 MPa at elevated temperature).
generation.baseline: The as‐cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy with density ~10.21 g/cm3, yield strength ~1600 MPa (room temperature) and ~855 MPa (elevated temperature)
generation.boundary: Yield strengths measured under standard tensile (or compressive) loading at room temperature and at approximately 1000 °C
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative trade-off between density reduction and mechanical strength retention is uncertain and must be confirmed experimentally, as the effect of Al on solid solution strengthening may vary with its concentration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a compositional series of alloys by gradually substituting Hf with Al in the baseline alloy (e.g., Hf1-xAlxMoTaTiZr where x = 0, 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3). Process all alloys under identical as-cast conditions, then perform density measurements and tensile tests at room temperature and ~1000 °C. Use XRD and SEM to confirm that the phase structure remains similar.
measurements: Phase and microstructure consistency via XRD/SEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If any alloy in the series exhibits a reduction in density of ~15% or more but concurrently shows a decline in yield strength by more than 10% relative to the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline, the hypothesis will be falsified.

High-Temperature Mechanical Properties of NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 Refractory High-Entropy Alloys

Abstract: AbstractThe NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 is a refractory multi-principal-element alloy with high strength and good ductility at room temperature. It is important for possible high-temperature applications to investigate the deformation mechanism of the NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy at different temperatures using tensile tests. In this investigation, the tensile tests were conducted at room temperature to 1273 K on sheet materials fabricated by cold rolling combined with annealing treatments. At 473 K, the NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy exhibited a high tensile ductility (12%). At a testing temperature range of 673~873 K, the ductility was reduced, but the yield strength remained above 800 MPa, which is rare in most other alloys. The TEM investigations revealed that a dislocation slip controlled the plastic deformation, and the degree of deformation was closely related to the dislocation density. The true stress–strain curves of the alloy under different deformation conditions were obtained by tensile deformation at different deformation temperatures (673~873 K) and strain rates (0.001~0.0005 s−1). Machine Learning-Based Strength Prediction for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys of the Al-Cr-Nb-Ti-V-Zr System

Abstract: AbstractThe aim of this work was to provide a guidance to the prediction and design of high-entropy alloys with good performance. New promising compositions of refractory high-entropy alloys with the desired phase composition and mechanical properties (yield strength) have been predicted using a combination of machine learning, phenomenological rules and CALPHAD modeling. The yield strength prediction in a wide range of temperatures (20–800 °C) was made using a surrogate model based on a support-vector machine algorithm. The yield strength at 20 °C and 600 °C was predicted quite precisely (the average prediction error was 11% and 13.5%, respectively) with a decrease in the precision to slightly higher than 20% at 800 °C. An Al13Cr12Nb20Ti20V35 alloy with an excellent combination of ductility and yield strength at 20 °C (16.6% and 1295 MPa, respectively) and at 800 °C (more 50% and 898 MPa, respectively) was produced based on the prediction.Keywords: high-entropy alloys, machine learning, prediction, strength, structure

Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Novel Lightweight TaNbVTi-Based Refractory High Entropy Alloys

Abstract: AbstractA series of novel lightweight TaNbVTi-based refractory high entropy alloys (RHEA) were fabricated through ball-milling and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The reinforced phase of TiO precipitates were in-situ formed due to the introduction of Al2O3 ceramic particles. The RHEA with 15% Al2O3 exhibits a high compressive yield strength (1837 MPa) and a low density (7.75 g/cm3) with an adequate ductility retention. The yield strength and density are 32% higher and 15% lower, respectively, compared to the RHEA without Al2O3 addition. The specific yield strength (237 MPa cm3/g) of the RHEAs is much higher than that of other reported RHEAs, and is mainly ascribed to the introduction of high volume fraction of Al2O3 additives, resulting in solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening. Meanwhile, the ductile matrix is responsible for the good compressive plasticity.Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, powder metallurgy, sintering, mechanical property

Conclusions: Novel lightweight TaNbVTi-based RHEAs has been successfully developed
